title: A shopping cart class
description:
Write a class `ShoppingCart` that keeps prices in whole cents:

```java
ShoppingCart cart = new ShoppingCart();
cart.add("Tea", 250, 2);          // name, unit price in cents, quantity
cart.add("Cake", 425, 1);
cart.add("tea", 250, 1);          // the same item (names ignore case): quantity becomes 3, the first name is kept
cart.itemCount();                 // 4: total quantity
cart.totalCents();                // 1175
cart.remove("TEA");               // true; false if not in the cart
cart.receipt();                   // see below
```

- `add` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a blank name, a negative price or a quantity below 1. Adding an existing item with a **different** price also throws.
- `receipt()` lists the items in the order they were first added, one per line, as `<name> x<qty> <line total>` with euros and 2 decimals (`Tea x3 7.50`), then `Total: <total>`. Lines end with `\n`. An empty cart gives just `Total: 0.00\n`.

Keep the items in a private list; you may write a small helper class for an item below `ShoppingCart` in the same file (only one class per file can be `public`). The class lives in `ShoppingCart.java`: in Java, a top-level class goes in a file with its own name.
hints: A small class `Item` with name, price and quantity, in the same file, keeps the list simple; a private `find(name)` method avoids repeating the case-insensitive search.
Multiply as `long`: one billion cents times 3 does not fit in an `int`.
